# Introduction {.unnumbered}

Since being proposed in *Attention is All You Need* by Vaswani et al. in 2017, the Transformer has become 
the standard backbone in almost every area of deep learning, ranging from NLP, vision, speech, and reinforcement learning 
. This document breaks down the Transformer into **three core ideas** — **token, 
attention, and positional encoding** — and 
organizes the information by answering the structural question of "why this structure is superior to RNN/CNN."

::: {.callout-tip}
## Wireless Communication Intuition One-Line Summary
**Attention is adaptive beamforming, Positional Encoding is 
pilot symbols, and Multi-head is MIMO multi-beam.** This correspondence 
is explained in detail throughout the text.
:::

---

# Two Intrinsic Difficulties of Sequence Modeling

Unlike *fixed-length snapshot* data such as images and graphs, **sequence data** (language, 
speech, video, time series) must solve the following two problems simultaneously.

| Problem | Description |
|---|---|
| **Long-term dependency** | A distant token determines the meaning of the current token |
| **Context** | Even the same token can have different meanings depending on the surrounding context |

> *"Buffalo buffalo Buffalo buffalo buffalo buffalo Buffalo buffalo."*
> — A grammatically correct English sentence consisting of 8 identical words. The meaning is entirely
> Depends on context.

RNN attempted to solve these two problems through sequential updates of the hidden state, but
- **Vanishing gradient**: Information from a distance is lost during the BPTT process
- **Sequential Processing**: Cannot be parallelized, inefficient GPU utilization

The Transformer bypasses this limitation with **attention that views the entire sequence at once**.

---

# First core idea: Token

## From neuron to token

The basic unit of existing neural networks was the **neuron**, which has a scalar value. 
The Transformer elevates the unit by one level and treats **vectors as the unit**.

$$
\text{Neuron: } x \in \mathbb{R}, \qquad \text{Token: } \mathbf{t} \in \mathbb{R}^{d}
$$

A token is an "**encapsulated bundle of information**." 
A single token contains all multidimensional attributes, such as meaning, location, and context.

::: {.callout-note}
## Relationship with GNN
a node feature or node attribute in Graph Neural Networks 
is a token in the Transformer world. They are essentially the same data structure.
:::

## How to tokenize input

| Input Type | Tokenization Method |
|---|---|
| **Image** | Cropped into 16×16 patches and projected each patch as a vector (ViT) |
| **Language** | Split into word/subword units and embedding |
| **Audio** | Project spectrogram slice of a constant window as a vector |

project each chunk onto a fixed-dimensional vector **.

## Linear combination of tokens and `.z` notation

A linear combination of neurons is a scalar weighted sum:

$$x_\text{out} = \sum_{i=1}^N w_i \, x_{\text{in}_i}$$

Linear combinations of tokens are essentially the same, but the notation differs because the unit is a vector:

$$t_\text{out}.\mathbf{z} = \sum_{i=1}^N w_i \, t_{\text{in}_i}.\mathbf{z}$$

::: {.callout-important}
## `.z` Meaning of the notation
`.z` is an indexing notation pointing to a specific element of a token vector. 
In other words, the above formula means *"The $z$-th element of the output token is the weighted sum of the $z$-th elements of the input tokens "*, which 
explicitly reveals that the same weight $w_i$ is applied to all elements .

Rewritten in vector notation, it is simple:
$$\mathbf{t}_\text{out} = \sum_{i=1}^N w_i \, \mathbf{t}_{\text{in}_i}$$
:::

This element-wise identical weight structure 
exactly matches the weighted sum of the values in attention.

---

# Second key idea: Attention

## Limitations of CNN: Locality Bias

CNNs are built on the **locality** assumption. $k \times k$ kernels always 
look only at adjacent pixels:

$$y_{ij} = \sum_{p=-k}^{k}\sum_{q=-k}^{k} w_{pq} \cdot x_{i+p,\, j+q}$$

This causes inherent difficulties in two tasks:

- **Global Counting**: "How many birds are in the image?" — The entire patch must be integrated
- **Long-distance relationship**: "Are the bird in the bottom left and the bird in the top right the same species?" — Two far apart
area must be **directly** compared

To establish long-distance relationships, you must stack layers deeply to expand the receptive field, but 
information becomes diluted in this process.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Wireless Communication Intuition
The locality of CNN is equivalent to **local cooperation where only nearby antennas cooperate**. 
On the other hand, attention is **cooperative MIMO where the entire cell shares CSI** — 
any two nodes directly exchange information without distance constraints.
:::

## Weight vs. Attention: Static vs. Dynamic

The **structural core** of Transformer excellence can be summarized in a single line:

::: {.callout-important}
## Core
**General weights are fixed after training, but attention weights 
are generated in real-time based on the input.**
:::

When compared using the formula:

$$
\text{일반 Weight: } y = \sum_i \underbrace{w_i}_{\text{고정}} \cdot x_i
\qquad
\text{Attention: } y = \sum_i \underbrace{\alpha_i(\mathbf{x})}_{\text{입력의 함수}} \cdot v_i
$$

$w_i$ is a point in the parameter space $\Theta$, but $\alpha_i$ is the **output of the function produced by the parameters 
**. This one-step meta-fication gives rise to all the superiority of the Transformer.

### Three capabilities created by dynamic weights

#### Context-dependent representation

Even the same token must have different expressions depending on the context.

```
"배가 고프다"  → 배 = 복부
"배가 떠난다"  → 배 = 선박
"배를 먹었다"  → 배 = 과일
```

With a fixed weight, "pear" always produces the same output. Since Attention 
changes $\alpha_j$ depending on surrounding tokens ("hungry", "leaves", "ate"), **the representation itself 
changes**. This is the essence of contextual embedding.

#### Adaptive receptive field

operates flexibly as follows depending on the data :

| Situation | Attention Behavior |
|---|---|
| Simple declarative | Focus on adjacent tokens (effectively local) |
| long-range demonstrative pronoun | long-range jump as antecedent |
| Counting task | Reference all tokens evenly |

**Same model, same parameters, but behavior changes depending on the data.**

#### Learned routing

The separation of Q, K, and V makes **"who asks what to whom"** learnable:

$$
\underbrace{Q}_{\text{무엇을 찾나?}} \cdot
\underbrace{K^\top}_{\text{무엇을 갖고 있나?}}
\;\to\; \underbrace{\alpha}_{\text{누구한테 얼마나?}}
\;\to\; \underbrace{\alpha V}_{\text{수집 결과}}
$$

::: {.callout-tip}
## Wireless Communication Intuition
- **Fixed weight = Fixed beamforming**: Beam direction is predetermined
- **Attention = Adaptive Beamforming**: Readjusts the beam direction at every moment based on the channel state (input).

Just as the beamforming weights $\mathbf{w}^*(\mathbf{h})$ are a function of the channel $\mathbf{h}$, 
the attention score $\alpha_i(\mathbf{x})$ is a function of the input $\mathbf{x}$.
:::

## Self-Attention: View as Matrix Operation

For the input token matrix $\mathbf{T}_\text{in} \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d}$ ($N$ tokens, each dimension $d$):

$$
\mathbf{Q} = \mathbf{T}_\text{in}\mathbf{W}_q^\top, \quad
\mathbf{K} = \mathbf{T}_\text{in}\mathbf{W}_k^\top, \quad
\mathbf{V} = \mathbf{T}_\text{in}\mathbf{W}_v^\top
$$

Split each token into query/key/value vectors using three trainable projection matrices $\mathbf{W}_q, \mathbf{W}_k, \mathbf{W}_v$ .

The attention matrix and output are:

$$
\mathbf{A} = \text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^\top}{\sqrt{m}}\right), \qquad
\mathbf{T}_\text{out} = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{V}
$$

where $m = d_k$ (dimension of the key vector).

::: {.callout-note}
## Why divide into $\sqrt{d_k}$
If the variance of $\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^\top$ increases in proportion to $d_k$, the softmax shifts toward extreme values and the gradient disappears. Dividing by $\sqrt{d_k}$ 
to keep the variance near 1 is the key to learning stability.
:::

### Meaning Interpretation

Self-attention is **"an operation that refines its own representation by considering neighboring tokens 
"**. It can be viewed as a process where a patch looks at its surrounding patches 
and re-determines "which part of the dog I am. "

Let's look at a VQA (Visual Question Answering) example:

| Query | Where Attention Focuses |
|---|---|
| "How many animals?" | All patches containing animals (uniformly distributed) |
| "What color is the impala?" | Focus only on the Impala patch |

Even with the same image, the attention distribution changes dynamically depending on the query. 
This is why attention is called "query-based dynamic pooling."

## Masked Attention

A variant that blocks a specific token from seeing other tokens:

$$
\text{MaskedAttn}(\mathbf{Q},\mathbf{K},\mathbf{V}) =
\text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^\top + \mathbf{M}}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)\mathbf{V}
$$

Mask $\mathbf{M}$ inserts $-\infty$ at the location to be blocked — after softmax it becomes 0 and 
is completely blocked.

**Most common use**: **causal mask** in decoders. Since looking at future tokens in autoregressive generation 
is cheating, all positions $j > i$ are masked.

$$M_{ij} = \begin{cases} 0 & j \leq i \\ -\infty & j > i \end{cases}$$

## Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA)

With a single $(Q, K, V)$ projection, it is easy to learn only one relationship pattern. Therefore, 
**multiple heads are operated in parallel**:

$$\text{MultiHead}(Q,K,V) = \text{Concat}(\text{head}_1, \ldots, \text{head}_h)\mathbf{W}^O$$

Each head has its own $(\mathbf{W}_q^{(i)}, \mathbf{W}_k^{(i)}, \mathbf{W}_v^{(i)})$ 
and calculates attention in a different subspace.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Wireless Communication Intuition: MIMO Beamforming
The $h$ heads are $h$ independent beams. Each beam 
is beamformed in a different direction (subspace) to simultaneously capture various channel states. 
The reason why multi-head attention is more expressive than general attention is exactly the same as the reason why **multi-beams have higher angular diversity than single beams** 
.
:::

It is also interesting in terms of interpretability — analyzing the learned heads 
reveals **specialization** where some heads establish grammatical relationships, others semantic relationships, and still others positional relationships .

---

# Third Key Idea: Positional Encoding

## The trap called Permutation Equivariance

Pure self-attention is **permutation equivariant**:

$$F_\theta(\text{permute}(\mathbf{T}_\text{in})) = \text{permute}(F_\theta(\mathbf{T}_\text{in}))$$

In other words, **shuffling the token order simply shuffles the output in the same way, without any loss of information.** 
Put another way, attention alone **ignores order information.**

This means that the result of shuffling the image patch and the original are encoded with the same expression 
, which is a fatal problem in languages where *"I love you"* and *"I love you"* 
have the same expression.

## Solution: Directly inject location information into the input

Add a unique vector for each position $pos$:

$$\text{PE}_{(pos, 2i)} = \sin\!\left(\frac{pos}{10000^{2i/d_\text{model}}}\right), \quad
\text{PE}_{(pos, 2i+1)} = \cos\!\left(\frac{pos}{10000^{2i/d_\text{model}}}\right)$$

Final input: $\mathbf{x}_\text{input} = \mathbf{x}_\text{embed} + \text{PE}$.

### Advantages of Sinusoidal PE

- **Extrapolability**: Provides reasonable positional representations even for long sequences never seen during training
- **Relative Position Encoding**: $\text{PE}_{pos+k}$ as a linear transformation of $\text{PE}_{pos}$
Representable → Model easily learns relative distance
- **Scale Variety**: Vibrating at different frequencies per dimension → From short distances to long distances
Capturing various patterns

::: {.callout-tip}
## Wireless Communication Intuition: Pilot Symbol
is essentially the same as the receiver in OFDM inserting **pre-agreed pilot symbols** into a specific subcarrier to estimate the channel .

- **Pilot** = A pre-known pattern that differs for each location
- **PE** = Deterministic sin/cos pattern that varies by location

Just as the receiver estimates the channel with a pilot, the Transformer 
estimates "where this token came from" with a PE.
:::

---

# Overall Architecture Summary

Now, combine the three ideas to complete the Encoder-Decoder structure of the original paper.

## Data Flow

```
Inputs
  └→ Input Embedding + Positional Encoding
       └→ [Encoder Block × N]
            ├ Multi-Head Self-Attention → Add & Norm
            └ Feed Forward          → Add & Norm
            ⇒ Encoder Output (다른 모든 디코더 블록의 K, V 공급원)

Outputs (shifted right)
  └→ Output Embedding + Positional Encoding
       └→ [Decoder Block × N]
            ├ Masked MH Self-Attention   → Add & Norm
            ├ Cross-Attention (Q←dec, K,V←enc) → Add & Norm
            └ Feed Forward               → Add & Norm
            ⇒ Linear → Softmax → Output Probabilities
```

## Meaning of Nx: Deep stacking

$$\mathbf{h}^{(l)} = \text{TransformerBlock}(\mathbf{h}^{(l-1)}), \quad l = 1, \ldots, N$$

The original paper was $N=6$, but modern LLMs have increased to $N=96$ (GPT-3) or higher. 
As the layers deepen, the representation becomes increasingly abstract:

| Layer | Representation being learned |
|---|---|
| Sub- (1~2) | Lexical, Grammatical Patterns |
| Infix (3~5) | Syntactic dependency, cross-reference |
| Upper (6~N) | Semantics, Inference, Task-Specific Patterns |

## Add & Norm: Residual Linking and Normalization

Each sublayer is wrapped in the following form:

$$\mathbf{x}' = \text{LayerNorm}(\mathbf{x} + \text{SubLayer}(\mathbf{x}))$$

- **Residual connection ($\mathbf{x} +$)**: acting as a gradient highway
Enables the learning of deep networks (ResNet principle). Also 
guarantees that original information is not lost.
- **Layer Normalization**: Ensures training stability by normalizing at the token level.
Unlike batch norm, it does not rely on inter-sample statistics, so 
it is suitable for variable-length sequences and RNN-like processing.

$$\text{LayerNorm}(\mathbf{x}) = \boldsymbol{\gamma} \odot \frac{\mathbf{x} - \mu}{\sigma + \epsilon} + \boldsymbol{\beta}$$

## Feed Forward Network (FFN)

2-layer MLP applied **independently** to each token:

$$\text{FFN}(\mathbf{x}) = \max(0, \mathbf{x}\mathbf{W}_1 + \mathbf{b}_1)\mathbf{W}_2 + \mathbf{b}_2$$

Dimensional change: $d_\text{model} \to d_{ff} \to d_\text{model}$ (usually $d_{ff} = 4 d_\text{model}$).

::: {.callout-note}
## Division of roles between Attention and FFN
- **Attention**: Information exchange **between** tokens — whose information to retrieve and how much
- **FFN**: Non-linear transformation **inside** the token — how to process the imported information

The essence of a Transformer block is that these two are stacked alternately.
:::

## Cross-Attention: Legs of Encoder ↔ Decoder

The decoder's second attention 
takes the **query from the decoder, and the key/value from the encoder**:

$$\mathbf{Q} = \mathbf{H}_\text{dec}\mathbf{W}_q, \quad
\mathbf{K} = \mathbf{H}_\text{enc}\mathbf{W}_k, \quad
\mathbf{V} = \mathbf{H}_\text{enc}\mathbf{W}_v$$

This single line determines **“where in the input sequence the decoder will refer when generating output tokens.”** In translation, the mechanism automatically learns a natural soft alignment, such as attending to the English word *“love”* when producing the corresponding target word.

## Meaning of "Outputs (shifted right)"

Teacher forcing method learning:

```
Target:  <BOS>  나는  밥을  먹었다  <EOS>
입력:    <BOS>  나는  밥을  먹었다       (마지막 제외)
출력:    나는   밥을  먹었다  <EOS>      (첫 토큰 제외)
```

During training, the decoder **predicts the next token by taking previous correct answer tokens as input**. 
During inference, since there are no correct answers, it **feeds back the previous predicted token** (autoregressive).

---

# MLP vs Transformer Comparison

| Item | MLP | Transformer (vanilla) |
|---|---|---|
| Basic unit | Neuron (Scalar) | Token (Vector) |
| Inter-token operation | linear (all inputs → all outputs) | self-attention (learned dynamic routing) |
| In-token operation | ReLU (neuron-wise) | MLP (token-wise) |
| Weight nature | Fixed after training | Recalculated every time depending on input |
| Sequential processing | Different weights per position | Permutation equivariant + PE |

Transformer 
can essentially be viewed as a structure that inserts attention instead of the linearity of an MLP. Attention 
bypasses the limitations of a static structure created by a linear transformation into a dynamic structure.

---

# Application: Language Model and GPT

## Definition of Language Model

Modeling the probability distribution of the next word given the previous words:

$$P(w_t \mid w_1, w_2, \ldots, w_{t-1})$$

Approximately fixed window assumption:

$$P(w_t \mid w_{t-n}, \ldots, w_{t-1})$$

As the scale increases, **Large Language Model (LLM)** — GPT, Claude, HyperCLOVA X, etc.

## GPT: Decoder-only Transformer

GPT(Generative Pretrained Transformer) is 
a structure that uses only the **decoder part** of the original paper.

- Remove Encoder, Remove Cross-attention
- **Use only causal masked self-attention**
- Pre-training with next token prediction

$$\mathcal{L} = -\sum_t \log P(w_t \mid w_{<t}; \theta)$$

The key finding of the GPT series is that training a massive corpus with this simple learning objective 
leads to emergent zero-shot/few-shot generalization ability.

::: {.callout-note}
## minGPT
Andrej Karpathy’s [minGPT](https://github.com/karpathy/minGPT) is an educational implementation of GPT in about 300 lines. It is useful for seeing how the concepts in the text map to code.
:::

---

# Limitations and Follow-up Research

## Computational complexity

The time/space complexity of self-attention for sequence length $n$ is:

$$O(n^2 \cdot d)$$

This is because it calculates the similarity of all token pairs. If the length is $n=10{,}000$, 100 million pairs 
are required.

## Absence of external Windows information

Information outside the window (context length) is **completely** invisible. While RNNs 
can theoretically handle infinite lengths (though in practice they cannot due to vanishing), Transformers 
have hard constraints.

## Direction of follow-up research

| Classification | Representative Technique | Key Idea |
|---|---|---|
| Sparse Attention | Longformer, BigBird | Calculate only some token pairs |
| Linear Attention | Performer, Linformer | $O(n)$ with kernel tricks |
| Long-context | FlashAttention | Practical acceleration with memory IO optimization |
| RNN-Transformer Hybrid | Mamba (SSM) | State-space model $O(n)$ + Infinite Context |

---

# Summary

::: {.callout-important}
## One-page summary

**Three Key Ideas**

1. **Token**: Elevate the basic unit of data from a scalar neuron to a vector token
2. **Attention**: Between tokens using **dynamic weights** that are recalculated every time based on the input
Routing information. QKV separation, scaled dot-product, multi-head, causal mask 
detailed design
3. **Positional Encoding**: at each position to break permutation equivariance
Add another deterministic signal to the input

**The Core of Structural Superiority**

> General weights are fixed in the parameter space, but the attention score is a function of the input.
> $w_i \in \Theta$ instead of $\alpha_i = f_\Theta(\mathbf{x})$. This one step of
> meta-ization, context-dependent representation, adaptive receptive field,
> produces all three superiorities known as learned routing.

**Wireless Communication Correspondence Table**

| Transformer Concept | Wireless Communication Support |
|---|---|
| Attention weight $\alpha_i(\mathbf{x})$ | Adaptive beamforming weight $\mathbf{w}^*(\mathbf{h})$ |
| Multi-head | MIMO Multi-beam, angular diversity |
| QK dot product | Channel alignment, matching filter |
| Positional Encoding | OFDM Pilot Symbol |
| Causal mask | causal system (causal filter) |
| FFN | Per-channel Non-linear Equalizer |
| Cross-attention | Transmitter-Receiver Cooperative Decoding |
:::
